mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown accelerating week-over-week decline (2.6, -0.1, -1.9, -11.4), indicating a momentum effect where the magnitude of decline compounds as fewer people engage in discretionary trips, pulling the 4-week mean further down.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weeks of declining RETAIL_REC with sharp acceleration in week t-0w
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean over the last 28 days despite the observed accelerating decline, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A collapse in TRANSIT mobility past a critical threshold signals that transit-dependent retail trips (commute-adjacent shopping) become structurally unavailable, suppressing RETAIL_REC for at least two weeks following the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -10 points from baseline in a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped to -14.3 at t-0w, the first week crossing -10
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rebounds within two weeks after TRANSIT first crosses -10, despite continued depressed transit use, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The joint occurrence of rising RESIDENTIAL (people sheltering at home) and falling WORKPLACES (reduced commuting) creates a compounding behavioral shift toward home-centered living that suppresses RETAIL_REC more severely than either series would independently predict.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 3.0 while WORKPLACES fell to -4.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not fall below its trailing mean even though RESIDENTIAL continues rising and WORKPLACES continues falling jointly, the interaction effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous steep declines across TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, PARKS, and RETAIL_REC in the final observed week indicate an active regime of tightening government restrictions (e.g., closures, stay-at-home guidance), under which RETAIL_REC is mechanically driven lower as non-essential activity is curtailed.
evidence_refs: fact:all four non-residential/non-grocery series fell sharply in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC recovers toward baseline over the next 4 weeks despite continued coincident declines in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and PARKS, the regime-driven mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp spike in GROCERY_PHARM (+9.3) in the most recent week reflects panic-buying/stockpiling behavior that front-loads essential shopping demand, causing a near-term further decline in RETAIL_REC as households reduce subsequent non-essential outings.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM jumped from 2.6 to 9.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following the GROCERY_PHARM spike rather than falling further, the stockpiling-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As mid-March transitions into early spring, rising seasonal temperatures typically increase outdoor and retail foot traffic; a rebound in PARKS mobility toward baseline would partially offset lockdown effects and limit further deterioration in RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mobility fluctuated but remained less negative than RETAIL_REC in prior weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline alongside RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks with no seasonal rebound, the seasonal offset hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES exceeding 4 points signals accelerating remote-work adoption, which reduces weekday lunch and after-work retail trips, producing a measurable decline in RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 0.3 to -4.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following two weeks after a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 4 points, the activity-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both collapsed sharply within a single week, this pattern is consistent with an already-enacted stay-at-home directive; under such a regime RETAIL_REC continues to fall in the immediate next week as compliance builds.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell to -14.3 and WORKPLACES to -4.4 in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the immediate next week despite the joint TRANSIT/WORKPLACES collapse, the lockdown-onset regime hypothesis is falsified.
